title: 🏛️ Exam 2025 · reading: a trip to Tunisia ⭐⭐

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2025 — reading, question 2, paragraph 1)
The exam gives a summary of the text with one word missing. Paragraph 1 says: "Annie's favourite hobby is reading, especially about the history of countries."

Complete the summary with ONE word from paragraph 1: "Annie knows a lot about the history, culture and monuments of many ___."

options.text: especially
different
favourite
countries

questions.explanation: The summary says what Annie knows about: the history, culture and monuments of many countries, which is the word the paragraph uses for the subject of her reading. The words especially, different and favourite come from the same paragraph, but after many the sentence needs a noun that names places with a history, and none of the three is a noun.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2025 — reading, question 2, paragraph 2)
Paragraph 2 says: "She won the prize."

Complete the summary with ONE word from paragraph 2: "Annie once participated in a competition and ___ a trip to Tunisia thanks to reading."

options.text: felt
won
worked
waiting

questions.explanation: The summary needs a verb in the past that can take a trip as its object, and the text says that Annie won the prize. Felt and worked are other verbs of the paragraph, but nobody felt or worked a trip, and waiting is not a past form.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2025 — reading, question 3, paragraph 2)
Paragraph 2 says: "A week later, Annie received an e-mail. What joy!"

How did Annie know that she was the winner of the prize?

options.text: She received an e-mail.
Her teacher told her at school.
She saw her name in a magazine.
A friend phoned her that night.

questions.explanation: The text says that a week later Annie received an e-mail, and her joy shows that the news was good: she learned from that e-mail that she had won. No teacher, magazine page or phone call is mentioned, so those answers only say what could happen in real life.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2025 — reading, question 1)
Annie's story has four events. Put them in the order in which they happen in the text.

options.text: Annie loved visiting museums in Tunisia.
Annie answered the questions about Tunisia.
Annie wanted to spend more time in Tunisia.
Annie was happy to win the trip to Tunisia.

questions.explanation: Annie first answered the questions about Tunisia, because the magazine offered the trip to anyone who could answer them. A week later she learned that she had won and she was happy. In Tunisia she enjoyed the museums, and at the end of the trip she wished she could stay longer.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2025 — reading, paragraphs 1 and 2)
Paragraph 1 says: "…a trip to Tunisia for anyone who could answer questions about its famous monuments." Paragraph 2 says: "She worked hard, reading every book about Tunisia."

Why did Annie read every book about Tunisia?

options.text: To find a job in the school library.
To answer the questions about its monuments.
Because her teacher asked her to read them.
To write her own travel magazine about Tunisia.

questions.explanation: The magazine offered the trip to anyone who could answer questions about the monuments of Tunisia, so Annie worked hard and read every book to be able to answer them. The text never speaks of a job, of a teacher's request or of a magazine that she wanted to write: those reasons are only likely guesses.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2025 — reading)
The text follows Annie from her school library to Tunisia. Which sentence tells what the whole text is mainly about?

options.text: A girl spends hours reading in her school library.
A travel magazine offers a prize about famous monuments.
A girl enjoys visiting the museums of Tunisia.
A girl who loves reading wins a trip to Tunisia.

questions.explanation: The whole text tells one story: a girl who loves reading wins a trip to Tunisia and enjoys it. The library, the prize of the magazine and the museums are true details of that story, but each of them covers only one part of the text.
